issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) expects a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) but the template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient) instead. The solution implements addToStockIngredients. This name mismatch will cause confusion and compilation errors if students implement SealSaloon or follow the UML and call addToStockIngredients on the provided Stock class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock class expose the method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (public) as shown in the UML and used in the solution. Concretely, rename the existing addItem(StockIngredient) method to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) or add a delegating addToStockIngredients method that calls addItem, so the template matches the problem specification and the solution.

issues.description: The Stock API method for adding a StockIngredient is named addToStockIngredients in the problem UML and the solution, but the template implementation exposes addItem(StockIngredient). This renaming of the same conceptual operation across artifacts can confuse students: the problem text and tests expect addToStockIngredients, while the starter code only provides addItem, forcing students to reconcile two different names for the same concept.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add a public wrapper addToStockIngredients that delegates to addItem) so the method name matches the problem statement UML and the solution implementation.
